title: Randomized calibration probes to detect JSON schema regressions under FP8/INT8 serving
creator: Ava Romero
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent structured-output regressions (missing fields, type drift, unexpected nulls) when serving quantized models with mixed FP8/INT8 profiles. Root causes span per-batch scale instability, token-level rounding artifacts, and KV-cache alignment differences introduced during calibration. Existing CI checks catch gross failures but miss subtle schema drift that only shows on realistic dialogue prefixes.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight, randomized calibration probe harness that runs during calibration and CI. The harness will: 1) run a curated set of tiny 'probe prompts' designed to elicit each schema field and edge-cases (empty arrays, optional keys, nested objects), 2) vary seed/temperature and small token-level perturbations to surface brittle behaviors, 3) capture deterministic fingerprints for each golden response using a canonical serialization + checksum (SHA256 hex), 4) compare probe outputs against golden fingerprints with configurable mismatch thresholds and per-field tolerances, and 5) automatically trigger targeted rollback or fallback to higher-precision variants when thresholds exceeded.

Why unique: Instead of blanket end-to-end golden comparisons, randomized probes focus on schema-sensitive token positions and calibration-time perturbations that mimic production variability. This approach is computationally cheap and catches regressions that only manifest under mixed-precision deployment and aggressive per-batch quant scales.
acceptance_criteria: Probe harness runs as part of calibration pipeline and CI (integration step), with <30s overhead per model/profile
For each quant profile (FP8/INT8 variants) we generate a set of probe fingerprints and store them in the calibration artifact store
CI fails when >3% of probes exceed field-level tolerances or when a required key is missing in any probe response
Automatic rollback flag is emitted and documented in the calibration report when mismatch thresholds are exceeded
Dashboard panel in Console shows probe pass/fail trends per model, quant profile, and calibration batch
test_plan: Create probe corpus covering top 50 schema fields across prioritized models (chat, structured-form, embedding meta)
Implement deterministic serializer that normalizes whitespace, sorts object keys for canonical checksum calculation
Add token-perturbation stage: ±1 token insertion/deletion and token-level bit-noise sim for quantization sensitivity
Run harness against baseline float32 models to generate golden fingerprints
Run harness against FP8 and INT8 calibration outputs across 5 calibration seeds; record mismatches and generate per-field diffs
Integrate failure cases into e2e regression tests and link failing PRs to the rollback policy
implementation_notes: Serializer must be language-agnostic (used by both runtime and CI); produce canonical JSON string before hashing
Fingerprint store will live alongside calibration artifacts (S3 path pattern: s3://redwood-calibration/{model}/{profile}/{build}/probes.jsonl)
Initial tolerances: missing-key = immediate fail; type-mismatch = fail; small numeric jitter within 1e-3 allowed for float fields
When a probe fails, capture full token-level trace + attention metadata if available for later root-cause analysis
Provide an opt-out config for low-risk models where any overhead is unacceptable
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives from non-deterministic generation. Mitigation: use deterministic seeds and normalize serialization before hashing.
Risk: Probe corpus coverage misses rare schema variants. Mitigation: expand corpus based on production telemetry of schema edge cases and user prompts.
Risk: Added calibration latency. Mitigation: probes are small and run in parallel; cap to target <30s per model/profile.
Risk: Storage growth for fingerprints. Mitigation: retention policy of 90 days and dedupe identical fingerprints across builds.
